title: Blizzard calls Forever WoW's biggest launch
summary: Blizzard says Forever set a new record for peak concurrent players and brought back more lapsed players than any previous WoW launch. No actual player numbers were shared. Queues stayed minimal even though each ruleset runs as one large regional world.

title: First players hit level 60 in about three days
summary: A five-player group made up of a Paladin, a Shaman and three Mages reached the cap together a little over three days after launch. They leveled mostly by pulling large packs and clearing them with area damage. At that point the nearest rival was still at level 54.

title: Hotfixes: Voidwalker health up, Tanning Rack requirement cut
summary: The November 6 hotfixes fix a range of class spells and tooltips, raise the Voidwalker's base health, and resolve spawn and leash problems in Maraudon, Blackmaw Hold and The Drowned City. The Tanning Rack now needs skill 125 instead of 140. The update also improves how far away you can see other players and their targets.

title: Class tuning set for Tuesday, November 10
summary: Blizzard has scheduled class changes for November 10 and may follow up on later Tuesdays. Hunter pets and Warlock Voidwalkers will get tougher, and Affliction damage-over-time spells are being made worth casting next to Wrack. Enhancement Shamans will be tuned so that Strength becomes their main stat.

title: Hotfixes: Plainsrunning nerfed in battlegrounds
summary: Plainsrunning stacks no longer accumulate, and they now drop off when the player picks up a battleground flag. Zephras Isle trade vendors now sell starter profession bags, and a Druid trainer was added on the island. Several quest NPCs now respawn faster.

title: First known-issues list: PvP vendors offline
summary: The day after launch, Blizzard posted a short list of known problems. The PvP vendors in Orgrimmar, Stormwind and Dalaran were temporarily unavailable. The list also covered a cauldron in Razorfen Kraul that can trap players, controller and UI bugs, and an Ashenvale quest that was turned off because it caused crashes.

title: Launch praised as unusually smooth
summary: Press coverage of launch night reported waits of only a few minutes and stable performance, even in crowded starting areas. Writers credited the new mega-server setup for handling the load. A Blizzard vice president described the early hours as going surprisingly well.

title: Roaming Orgrimmar vendor sells a wolf pup pet
summary: A new wandering vendor in Orgrimmar sells the Prairie Wolf Pup Carrier for 60 silver. She moves around the city, so finding her can take some searching.

title: World of Warcraft: Forever is live
summary: Forever launched worldwide at 3 p.m. PST on November 4 (23:00 UTC), and all beta and stress-test progress was wiped. New players pick a Classic or Enhanced experience preset, then choose a ruleset rather than a realm. Raids open on December 9, and Hardcore will arrive later.

title: Discord guild chat bridge and gamepad improvements
summary: Players can now link their Discord and WoW accounts and mirror guild chat in both directions, in Forever and in modern WoW. Blizzard also highlighted improvements to gamepad targeting, casting, looting and menu navigation.

title: Twitch drop: Pouch of Violet Dust toy
summary: Watching eligible WoW streams between November 4 and November 12 (4:30 p.m. PST) earns the Pouch of Violet Dust toy. It works only in Forever, and only during the launch celebration event. It is removed from collections once the event ends.

title: Taldramir revealed as Forever's first legendary
summary: About an hour before launch, Blizzard showed Taldramir, the Whispering Wood, as a physical 3D-printed staff during a live stream. A companion video shows Wētā building the prop. Observers expect it to come from the raids that open in December.

title: Final pre-launch notes: damage up, mob health up
summary: A large set of development notes raised damage for many classes and gave higher-level creatures more health to compensate. Training costs were evened out to about 206 gold in total from 1 to 60. Bags now have to be equipped manually, and respawns in starter zones were sped up for launch.

title: Podcast episode 6 covers the tech
summary: The sixth official podcast focused on the technology behind Forever, with a guest joining the developers. It was the last episode before launch.

title: Fix coming for over-strict name filter
summary: The name checker was rejecting valid names that happened to contain certain letter sequences. Blizzard confirmed the bug and said a fix would arrive with realm restarts.

title: Early name reservation opens
summary: Pack owners could create up to three characters to hold their names before launch, on a first-come, first-served basis. The window ran until November 3. Each name is a first name plus a surname that must be unique within the region.

title: Gold for carries must be paid directly
summary: Blizzard warned that gold paid for boosts or carries has to go straight from the buyer to the person providing the service. Routing it through a third party may lead to enforcement action.

title: Last racial pass before launch
summary: A final revision of racial abilities partly reverses the mid-October rework. Weapon-skill racials remain removed.

title: Beta ends after five weeks
summary: Blizzard closed the beta, thanked testers and said it would focus on the most important issues before launch. On the final day, a one-off celebration took over the starting zones.

title: Open stress test for everyone
summary: The October 21 stress test needed no subscription or beta invite, so anyone could log in. It ran on production hardware, and all characters and guilds were deleted afterwards ahead of name reservations.

title: Camping system explained
summary: Cooking fires can be upgraded into campfires where nearby players add profession-made features that give buffs. You have to sit or craft at the camp for a minute to receive them. Larger campfires and high-end features come from later skill levels and from dungeon drops.

title: Nine new dungeons and three raids confirmed
summary: Blizzard listed nine new five-player dungeons for levels 13 to 60, alongside reworked original dungeons. At 60, Barrow Deeps (10 players), Hyjal Summit (20) and a returning Onyxia's Lair (40) will be available.

title: Stress test moved to October 21
summary: The stress test was pushed back from October 19 to October 21. Blizzard also said that art datamined from recent beta builds is not meant for Forever.

title: Beta build reworks racial abilities
summary: The October 15 beta build rebuilt many racial traits and made changes to several classes. Some of these changes were later reversed before launch.

title: Temporary Economy Holds target gold buyers
summary: Accounts suspected of real-money gold trading can be temporarily cut off from trading, mail, guild banks and the Auction House. A hold carries no permanent penalty unless the activity is confirmed.

title: Beta build adds Dalaran dungeon, more dungeon XP
summary: This build increased experience from dungeons and opened a new Dalaran dungeon for testing. It also adjusted Rage generation and Penance.

title: Class deep dives, PvP ranks and Skyborne druid forms
summary: Blizzard published deep dives for Mage, Shaman, Rogue and Warlock, and explained PvP progression built on Honor and Rank Points. It also announced revised Skyborne druid forms and said SD versions would come in early 2027.

title: Beta level cap rises to 30
summary: A beta update raised the level cap to 30 and added another dungeon, along with class tuning and changes to PvP and experience gain. Blizzard also announced a wave of bans for botting and gold selling.

title: Class deep dives: Hunter, Druid, Priest, Warrior
summary: The first class articles covered changes to Hunter pets and Aimed Shot, Druid forms, Priest baseline abilities, and Warrior Rage. They also confirmed that respecs are now done at class trainers.

title: Collector's Edition contents revealed
summary: Blizzard listed what is in the physical Collector's Edition, including its digital codes, and gave restock details. It is sold through the Blizzard Gear Store while supplies last.

title: Legacy System replaces achievements
summary: Completing account-wide challenges earns Legacy Points, which each character spends in its own perk trees for professions, adventure and resourcefulness. At launch there are 65 challenges, and each character can spend up to 16 points. Cosmetic rewards unlock as your total grows.

title: Six new race and class combinations
summary: Orc Mage, Troll Warlock, Undead Paladin, Human Hunter, Gnome Priest and Dwarf Shaman are all playable in Forever. Several racial traits were updated to fit them.

title: Meet the Skyborne
summary: The new Skyborne race is descended from Highborne who made a pact with air spirits in Skywall. Players choose the Horde-aligned Windshapers or the Alliance-aligned High Order when creating a character. Both start on Zephras Isle, which covers levels 1 to 12.

title: Names now have two parts
summary: Every character has a first name and a surname, and the full combination must be unique across the whole region. Filters check both parts together, and surnames can be hidden on nameplates.

title: Beta opens
summary: The beta began on September 17. Epic Pack and Collection owners had guaranteed access, and others could opt in for a chance to play. Its level cap was later raised to 30.

title: Rulesets replace realms
summary: Instead of choosing a realm, players pick a ruleset: Normal, PvP, Roleplay or Roleplay PvP, with Hardcore coming later. Grouping, guilds and instances only work within the same ruleset and faction, while battlegrounds can mix rulesets.

title: Older graphics cards no longer supported
summary: Forever requires at least AMD GCN 1, NVIDIA Maxwell or Intel Skylake graphics, or newer. Blizzard says dropping older cards is what makes the updated visuals possible.

title: Forever announced at BlizzCon 2026
summary: Blizzard announced World of Warcraft: Forever as a permanent third version of the game that stays at level 60 and adds new zones, dungeons, quests and a new race. It is included with a regular subscription or Game Time. Three Skyborne packs went on sale the same day.

title: Roadmap: raids on December 9, more in 2027
summary: A BlizzCon panel recap put the first raid unlock on December 9. Hardcore, new raids and dungeons, a revamped classic raid and PvP season refreshes are planned through 2027.
